note: Generated by learning/tools/coverage_curve.py from metrics/replay-mix.json. EVERY MIX IS A STATED ASSUMPTION (plan §5.3); coverage is measured by runtime replay; decisions are counted, never timed.

curves.label: every corpus line weighted equally
curves.ASSUMPTION: Traffic is distributed like the fixture files: each of the 1,316 four-vendor corpus lines carries the same weight. Known to be false as a traffic model — fixtures are collections of parser test cases, roughly one line per case, so rare message types are heavily over-represented. It is here because it assumes nothing beyond the corpus and is the least favourable declared mix.

curves.label: four sources at 25 % each; within a source, by corpus line count
curves.ASSUMPTION: The four sources contribute equal volume; inside a source, strata keep their corpus proportions. Removes the accident that the PAN-OS fixtures are 40 % of all corpus lines; still inherits the over-representation of rare message types inside each source.

curves.label: four sources at 25 %; 80 % of each firewall's volume is connection/traffic logging
curves.ASSUMPTION: A firewall logs every connection, and management, threat and system events are comparatively rare: 80 % of each source's volume is assigned to its connection-class strata and 20 % to everything else, by corpus line count inside each class. The 80 % is a round number chosen by us, not taken from any capture; this is the mix most favourable to ULPF because the onboarded families are connection-class. Quote it only beside the other two.

curves.label: the demo's own stream: only the nine onboarded families, in the demo's proportions
curves.ASSUMPTION: Traffic consists of the nine onboarded families and nothing else, in the proportions of the demo's mixed capture (scripts/p6-build-packs.sh). Two of its pools are OURS, not corpus: the worked trace's Squid sample and the synthetic 11-slot Squid family built to show propagation. Coverage reaches ~100 % by construction; it shows the cost side of the curve and the one place propagation acts, and it is not evidence about live traffic.
